claims.text: The `protect` resource option is a Pulumi-engine construct that is enforced entirely within Pulumi and never sent to the cloud provider.
Many cloud resources carry their own, separate deletion-protection attributes that the cloud provider enforces independently of anything Pulumi knows about.
A GCP Cloud SQL instance has a `deletionProtection` attribute that is a cloud-provider-level deletion-protection setting separate from Pulumi's `protect` option.
An AWS RDS instance has a `deletionProtection` attribute that is a cloud-provider-level deletion-protection setting separate from Pulumi's `protect` option.
A resource can be unprotected in Pulumi and still refuse to delete because of the cloud provider's own deletion-protection attribute.
A resource can be protected in Pulumi while not having the cloud provider's own deletion-protection attribute enabled.

The page /docs/iac/operations/troubleshooting/destroy-failures/#deletion-protection-on-the-resource-itself exists and explains how to distinguish Pulumi's `protect` option from the cloud resource's own deletion protection and how to resolve each.
Pulumi has no single flag to protect every resource in a stack.
Stack transforms can be used to set the `protect` option on every resource in a stack as it's registered.
The `protect` resource option guards a resource within Pulumi.
Many cloud resources carry their own, separate deletion-protection attributes that the cloud provider or cloud API enforces independently of Pulumi.
A GCP Cloud SQL instance has a `deletionProtection` attribute enforced by the provider or cloud API independently of Pulumi's `protect` option.
An AWS RDS instance has a `deletionProtection` attribute enforced by the provider or cloud API independently of Pulumi's `protect` option.
Pulumi's `protect` resource option and a cloud resource's native deletion-protection attribute are complementary layers rather than substitutes for one another.

The page's 'Deletion protection on the resource itself' section (linked at /docs/iac/operations/troubleshooting/destroy-failures/#deletion-protection-on-the-resource-itself) explains how to distinguish Pulumi's `protect` option from a resource's own deletion-protection attribute and how to resolve a destroy failure caused by either.
The `retainOnDelete` resource option takes the opposite approach from `protect`.
The `retainOnDelete` resource option lets Pulumi remove a resource from state without calling the provider's delete operation, leaving the underlying cloud resource in place.
`retainOnDelete` is the right choice when you want to stop managing a resource with Pulumi, or hand it off, without destroying its data.
A `pulumi destroy` failure is often caused by the resource itself being guarded against deletion rather than by an engine problem, and the guard must be removed before Pulumi can delete the resource.
There are three distinct layers that can hold deletion protection on a resource.
Pulumi's `protect` resource option is an engine-level guard that never reaches the cloud provider.
An error naming a URN and mentioning `protect` indicates the `protect` resource option is set on that resource.

Some Pulumi providers refuse to issue the delete call at all when a resource carries a deletion-protection attribute, for example `deletionProtection` on `gcp.sql.DatabaseInstance` or `gcp.container.Cluster`.
When a Pulumi provider enforces a deletion-protection attribute, the failure surfaces from the provider before any request reaches the cloud API.
Some clouds reject the delete call themselves independent of Pulumi, for example AWS RDS `deletionProtection`, EC2 `disableApiTermination`, or an Azure Resource Manager management lock.
When a cloud API enforces deletion protection, the error text comes back from the cloud provider's API, often with a distinct error code such as `ScopeLocked`.
The remediation for provider-enforced and cloud-API-enforced deletion protection is the same.
`pulumi destroy` deletes what is already recorded in the stack's state, not what the program currently says.
Setting a deletion-protection attribute to `false` only in the Pulumi program is not enough on its own to allow `pulumi destroy` to succeed.
To remove provider- or cloud-API-enforced deletion protection, you must set the deletion-protection attribute to `false` in the Pulumi program, then run `pulumi up`, then run `pulumi destroy`.
Running `pulumi up` after changing a deletion-protection attribute propagates the change to both the live resource and Pulumi's state.
If deletion protection was already disabled outside of Pulumi (e.g., directly in the cloud console), `pulumi refresh` synchronizes the stack's state with reality.
After `pulumi refresh` synchronizes state when protection was disabled outside of Pulumi, `pulumi destroy` then succeeds without needing an intervening `pulumi up`.
The `gcp.sql.DatabaseInstance` resource has a `deletionProtection` attribute that is provider-enforced.
The `gcp.sql.DatabaseInstance` resource has a nested `settings.deletionProtectionEnabled` attribute that also guards the instance at the GCP API level.
The `gcp.container.Cluster` resource has a `deletionProtection` attribute that is provider-enforced.
The `gcp.bigquery.Table` resource has a `deletionProtection` attribute that is provider-enforced.
The `gcp.bigquery.Dataset` resource has a `deleteContentsOnDestroy` attribute.
Destroying a `gcp.bigquery.Dataset` that still contains tables fails unless `deleteContentsOnDestroy` is set to `true`.
The `aws.rds.Instance` and `aws.rds.Cluster` resources have a `deletionProtection` attribute that is enforced by the AWS API.
The `deletionProtection` attribute on `aws.rds.Instance` / `aws.rds.Cluster` defaults to `false`.
The `aws.s3.BucketV2` resource has a `forceDestroy` attribute.
The `forceDestroy` attribute on `aws.s3.BucketV2` defaults to `false`.
A non-empty `aws.s3.BucketV2` bucket fails to delete unless `forceDestroy` is set to true.
The `aws.ec2.Instance` resource has a `disableApiTermination` attribute that is enforced by the AWS API (EC2 termination protection).
The `aws.dynamodb.Table` resource has a `deletionProtectionEnabled` attribute that is enforced by the AWS API.
The `deletionProtectionEnabled` attribute on `aws.dynamodb.Table` defaults to `false`.
Azure resources under a management lock are represented in Pulumi by `azure-native.authorization.ManagementLockByScope` and scope-specific variants such as `ManagementLockAtResourceLevel`.
Azure management locks are enforced by Azure Resource Manager.
A `CanNotDelete` lock must be removed before an Azure resource under it can be deleted, independent of anything in the Pulumi program.
The `azure-native.keyvault.Vault` resource supports soft delete and purge protection.
Destroying an `azure-native.keyvault.Vault` only soft-deletes it.
Recreating an Azure Key Vault with the same name fails with a `VaultAlreadyExists` error until the soft-deleted vault is purged or recovered.
Purge protection on an Azure Key Vault prevents purging until its retention period elapses.
